newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Troy Resources races higher on results.
newsitem.headline: Troy Resources races higher on results.

text.p: Gold explorer Troy Resources NL put some shine on an otherwise dull gold sector on Friday after well-received drilling results from its Cornishman joint venture in Western Australia.
By 10.45 a.m. (0045 GMT), Troy shares had leapt 34 percent higher to A$1.35, their highest level since October 1987, on turnover of 99,533 shares.
"They have been the shining light in an otherwise dormant gold sector in the last week," said broker Dirk Van der Struyf of Hartley Poynton.

Troy's results from its drilling programme saw intercepts ranging from three metres at 43 grams per tonne (g/t) to five metres at 3.03 g/t and included intercepts of seven metres at 15.7 g/t and 10 metres at 11.40 g/t.
"They are excellent results," Van Der Struyf said, adding that further data was eagerly awaited.
"There is plenty of follow up drilling to do so that may prove interesting as well."
Troy holds 49 percent of the Cornishman joint venture while manager and operator Sons of Gwalia owns 51 percent.
Sons of Gwalia shares were two cents lower A$5.90 at 11.15 a.m. (0115 GMT).
